findings.problem: MetricWorkflow uses no state machine at all — status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms are independent fields that permit any combination including invalid ones such as is_sent=true with status not equal to 'sent', or is_validated=false with is_sent=true.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct or mutate MetricWorkflow into an impossible lifecycle state (e.g. validated-but-not-sent then sent with a stale status string), breaking invariants silently.
findings.fix: Replace all lifecycle fields with a single enum typestate, e.g. `enum MetricState { Pending { id: MetricId } , Validated { id: MetricId } , Sent { id: MetricId, sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }`. Each variant owns the data it needs; invalid combinations are unrepresentable.

findings.problem: status is a pub String field. The mark_sent function sets it to a magic-string literal. Any code can set status to any string value, including 'pending', '', or garbage, with no compile-time enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set status to any value, making status a lie. Pattern-matching on status with string comparison is fragile and cannot be exhaustive; the compiler cannot enforce that every lifecycle branch is handled.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with a domain enum `MetricState` with explicit variants (Pending, Validated, Sent). The mark_sent function should accept a Validated state and return a Sent state.

findings.problem: is_validated is a pub bool field. Together with is_sent (line 5), it forms a 4-state product space (2x2) but the actual lifecycle is a strict progression (Pending → Validated → Sent). Booleans cannot encode directionality or prevent going backwards.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can flip is_validated=true then is_validated=false (regression), or set is_sent=true while is_validated=false (skipping validation). The compiler treats booleans as independent bits with no lifecycle ordering.
findings.fix: Fold is_validated and is_sent into the MetricState enum variants. Validated becomes a variant with no sent_at_epoch_ms; Sent becomes a variant that requires it. Transitions go through functions that consume one state and produce the next.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is Option<u64> separate from the lifecycle booleans. It can be Some(...) when is_sent=false (stale timestamp), or None when is_sent=true (missing required data), or Some(...) when status is not 'sent'.
findings.failure_mode: The Option field creates invalid combinations with the independent booleans: stale timestamps on non-sent items, or missing timestamps on sent items. These are silent logical errors with no runtime check.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 into the Sent variant of the MetricState enum. Only a Sent state can carry a sent_at_epoch_ms, and it is guaranteed to be present (u64, not Option<u64>).

findings.problem: id is a raw pub String. There is no domain newtype for metric identifiers, so any string — empty, malformed, or from untrusted input — can become a MetricWorkflow id without validation.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid metric IDs (empty strings, duplicates, or hostile inputs) can be stored directly. The domain core cannot rely on id having any invariants (uniqueness, format, non-emptiness) because there is no smart constructor or newtype gate.
findings.fix: Define `pub struct MetricId(String)` (or better, a fixed-format newtype) with a smart constructor `fn new(id: &str) -> Result<MetricId, ParseError>` that validates non-emptiness and format. Use MetricId in the struct/enum instead of String.

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String for id, String for status, bool fields, Option<u64>) cross the parse boundary directly into the domain struct. There are no smart constructors, no fallible parsing, and no parse boundary — callers can construct MetricWorkflow with invalid domain state directly.
findings.failure_mode: The domain type is constructible from hostile inputs without any validation. The MetricWorkflow struct exposes all fields as pub, so there is no encapsulation and no way to enforce invariants at construction time.
findings.fix: Define MetricState enum with smart constructors (e.g. `MetricState::new_pending(id: MetricId) -> Self`) and remove all pub fields from the domain type. Raw DTOs from the shell boundary are parsed once via fallible constructors into trusted domain types before the core sees them.

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The code has six BLOCKER-level typestate violations: no enum state machine, status as String, lifecycle booleans, Option detached from lifecycle, raw String id, and no parse boundary. Every illegal combination of status/validated/sent/timestamp is representable and mutable by any caller. The mark_sent function is a pure mutation with no validation. Delivery is blocked until the typestate enum, smart constructors, and parse boundary are implemented.
